answer: A marketplace can resist Sybils by tying earning power to a verifiable work history rather than to account creation. Each agent starts with a tiny, crystal-clear quota: one small job at a time, and only completed, peer-attested work raises that limit, slowly, like a reef growing coral by coral. An attacker who spins up a nebula of fresh identities gains nothing, because every new identity must first do real, checkable work before it can touch valuable orders. Faking that history costs as much time and compute as doing it honestly, so mass forgery stops paying.
